To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the laser scanner is a good and fast instrument to survey a non-planar surface like the mosaic floor; 2) the 3D modeling of such a surface is possible by using the photogrammetric data and the laser data; 3) the 3d photorealistic modeling of such a floor is possible by using 3D textures; 4) the virtual navigation of a floor like that is possible.
a 3D photogrammetric survey is a good alternative to the laser scanner survey for the 3D modeling of a non-planar surface like the Theodorian mosaic floor.

the laser scanning and photogrammetry are two different techniques that can be applied to survey and model non-planar surfaces, the 3d photorealistic modeling is an effective technique that can be used to create a virtual tour of such surfaces and the virtual tour can be used to show thematic routes of the surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects: (1) the surveying, (2) the modeling, and (3) the navigation.

the following issues: 1) the acquisition of 3D data of the mosaic floor; 2) the creation of a 3D model of the surface; 3) the definition of a navigation system; 4) the creation of the thematic tours; 5) the integration of the virtual model in the real environment; 6) the creation of an interactive virtual tour.
the use of the 3D modeling of the mosaic floor to improve the knowledge of this important archaeological monument and the use of the virtual reality to improve the visit and the comprehension of it.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the virtual reality technology is an extremely useful instrument in the study and the conservation of ancient monuments.
the virtual reality technology is an excellent and innovative tool for the surveying and the 3D representation of complex surfaces and for the creation of virtual tours.
the virtual reconstruction of this mosaic floor, as well as the virtual tour, is a powerful instrument to understand and to enjoy the various parts, and the various themes of this mosaic floor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, thanks to the use of the new technology of laserscanning and the new software for the photorealistic rendering, the Thodorian floor has become an accessible and explorable virtual tour.
we have developed a new methodology for surveying, modeling and navigating the Theodorian mosaic floor of the Aquilea Basilica.

the mosaic floor of the Aquileian basilica has been virtually reconstructed in a way that the visitor can navigate through its 18th century state, with a high degree of detail and accuracy, as if he were actually there.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of 3D modeling and virtual reality technologies in archaeology can be very helpful in the study, the interpretation and the fruition of the archaeological remains.
the use of laser scanner and photogrammetry can be a valid and effective tool in the survey of non-planar surfaces.
the 3D model and the virtual navigation are useful tools to understand the complex structure of the mosaic floor and its historical and artistic meaning.
